source.title: DateTime.diffTo() silently returns undefined for the units weekday, weekNumber and yearDayNumber

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
n8n version: master at 59604870 (2026-11-19). Affects both expression engines (legacy
`n8n-workflow` and the isolated `@n8n/expression-runtime` engine: VM and QuickJS).

### Describe the problem

`DateTime.diffTo()` accepts a unit or an array of units. The code validates each unit against a
set built from `dateParts` and `durationUnits`. `dateParts` contains the `extract()` parts
`weekday`, `weekNumber` and `yearDayNumber`, which are not valid Luxon `diff()` units. These
three names therefore pass the validation and reach Luxon, which throws an internal
`InvalidUnitError`. The expression sandbox only forwards `ExpressionError` and
`ExpressionExtensionError` instances, so the internal error is swallowed and the expression
silently evaluates to `undefined`.

For any other unknown unit, for example `fortnight`, the function throws the intended friendly
error: `Unsupported unit 'fortnight'. Supported: 'milliseconds', ...`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the expression editor.
2. Evaluate `={{ DateTime.fromISO("2024-03-30T18:49:00Z").diffTo("2024-03-25T18:49:00Z", "weekday") }}`.
3. The result is `undefined`. The same happens for `weekNumber` and `yearDayNumber`.
4. Compare with `={{ ...diffTo(..., "fortnight") }}`, which throws the friendly error.

### Expected behavior

The three get-only parts should fail the unit check like any other unsupported unit and throw
`Unsupported unit 'weekday'. Supported: ...`, in both engines.

### Actual behavior

The expression silently evaluates to `undefined` in the legacy, VM and QuickJS engines.

### Root cause

`diffTo()` in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/date-extensions.ts` and its mirror in
`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/date-extensions.ts` builds the allowed-unit set
from `dateParts` and `durationUnits`, but only the `durationUnits` (and their singular forms,
which Luxon normalizes) are valid `diff()` units.

I have a small fix ready (friendly Unsupported-unit error in the two mirrored date-extensions files, regression tests included) and will link a PR here shortly. (Prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant; verified red→green across the three expression engines.)

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked both implementations at the reported commit: diffTo() builds allowedUnitSet from dateParts and durationUnits in packages/workflow/src/extensions/date-extensions.ts and packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/date-extensions.ts. Since dateParts also contains weekday, weekNumber, and yearDayNumber, validating against durationUnits alone would reject these extraction-only values before calling Luxon. Please keep the fix mirrored in both files.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text:
Great catch and spot-on root-cause analysis.

Restricting `diffTo()` validation strictly to `durationUnits` (and their singular forms) makes complete sense so it fails fast with an `ExpressionExtensionError` rather than hitting Luxon's unhandled `InvalidUnitError`.

Looking forward to the PR—feel free to link it here once opened!
